description:
## Goal

Ensure the order of `CallableFacts.direct_surfaces` is never allowed to make a transport product, artifact, diagnostic, or runtime answer depend on `ShapeId` interning order.

## Current state

At origin/main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`, one raw `ShapeId` packaging sort remains:

    src/compiler2/jobs/transport.rs:139-141
    draft.direct_surfaces.sort_by_cached_key(
        |surface| surface.iter().map(|shape| shape.as_u32()).collect::<Vec<_>>()
    );

`ShapeId` is an index in the World-owned shape interner, so `as_u32` is mint order, not structural identity.

This path is genuinely exercised by a non-singleton set: under LLDB,
`compiler2_transport_plan_projects_enum_reduce_bridge_callable_flow_by_producer_identity_over_range`
reaches this exact sort with `draft.direct_surfaces.len == 2`.

The former second occurrence in `surface_shapes` is closed by fz-kdt.108.
`surface_shapes` now preserves the `CallableSurface` walk order because its result is
zipped positionally with those surfaces when boundaries are published. Sorting
those rows by `ShapeId` was not merely cosmetic: it could hand one surface another
surface's shapes and caused the demonstrated members/boundary desynchronization.
Do not reintroduce a sort there.

## Current impact

No observable leak from the remaining finish-time `direct_surfaces` sort is
demonstrated on the current tree.

All traced production consumers treat `direct_surfaces` as membership:

- `TransportFactsBuilder` merging deduplicates with `contains`.
- `aggregate_callable_owners` unions with `contains`.
- backend reachability reads `CallableFacts.resolutions`, not `direct_surfaces`.
- `BackendProgram` canon does not render `RootBackendProductAnswer.transport`.

The transport regression oracle also compares direct surfaces set-wise through
`transport_surfaces_match_upstream`. Current focused transport/canon tests pass.

## Signal

Do not build a recursive `ShapeId` comparator merely because this raw-id sort
exists. Build this ticket only when one of these is supplied:

1. a schedule or shape-mint perturbation that changes an observable artifact,
   product settlement, diagnostic, or answer through this remaining sort; or
2. a new positional/order-sensitive consumer of `CallableFacts.direct_surfaces`.

A valid regression must contain more than one direct surface and must prove the
perturbation changes `ShapeId` mint order while semantic shape descriptors remain
the same.

## Strategy if the signal appears

First determine whether `direct_surfaces` is semantically a set. If it is, remove
the ordering authority from the representation or canonicalize only at an
actual presentation/persistence boundary. If it truly requires a stable vector
order, add one canonical structural comparator over `ShapeDescr`, recursively:

- `Nothing`
- `Lane`, compared by the canonical `LaneDescr` identity
- `Tuple`, lexicographically by child shapes
- `Callable`, compared by canonical `CallableDescr` identity

The comparator must not fall back to `ShapeId`, `LaneId`, `CallableId`, `BoundaryId`,
`Ty`, or `FunctionId` mint order. Add a red-first multi-surface perturbation gate
on the exact consumer that leaked.

## Related but separate raw-ID corners

The wrapper-owner tie fallback and the `CallableId`/`BoundaryId` packaging sorts
previously appended to this ticket are different interner domains and need
their own demonstrated signals. They should not expand a `ShapeId` fix without a
repro tying them to the same observable.
title: ShapeId mint-order remains in CallableFacts.direct_surfaces packaging; exercised but no observable consumer depends on the order
